subject: One question fingerprints any LLM — Cursor cut agent costs from $10K t
intro: AI is getting better at doing things without being told how. Cursor's agents rebuilt SQLite from a manual alone. NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 Edge gives robots a brain they carry on-device. Researchers fingerprint any LLM with a single question. The pattern? Less scaffolding, more autonomy. And the cost curve is bending fast: Cursor cut agent costs 15x just by being smarter about which model does what. We're watching capability compound quietly. Pay attention.

news.headline: Dev rebuilds Palantir's million-dollar war room and releases it free on GitHub
news.body: Palantir sells governments a war room that costs millions. Someone just built the same thing, put it on GitHub, and gave it away for free. It's called World Monitor . You get a live 3D globe pulling from 500+ news feeds across 15 categories, with AI summarizing everything as it lands. Military movements, economic shocks, cyber incidents, shipping lanes, flight paths. To get started: git clone the repo, npm install, npm run dev. That's it. No environment variables required out of the box. The repo already has 61k stars . It's fully open source under AGPL-3.0, so you can self-host it, fork it, or build on top of it.
bullets: 56 map layers you can stack on top of each other
A stress score for 31 countries that updates in real time
29 stock exchanges, commodities, and crypto in one panel
Local AI via Ollama, meaning zero API keys needed
Native desktop app for Windows, macOS, and Linux

news.headline: Cursor's agent team rebuilt SQLite in Rust from its 835-page manual, passing 100% of tests
news.body: Cursor gave a swarm of AI agents an 835-page SQLite manual and said: build this from scratch in Rust. No source code. No internet. No test suite. Just the docs. The result? A fully working database that passed 100% of a hidden test suite it had never seen. That is not a small thing. Here is how it works. The swarm splits into two roles: This split matters because a single agent trying to hold the whole project in its head eventually loses track. Splitting the roles keeps each agent focused. The big money insight: every model combo hit similar quality, but costs swung 15x , from $1,339 to $10,565. Using a frontier model only for planning, and a cheap model for the actual coding, slashed worker costs from $9,373 down to $411. You can explore the output yourself at github.com/anysphere/minisqlite.
bullets: Planner agents use smart, expensive models to break the big goal into smaller tasks and delegate them.
Worker agents use faster, cheaper models to actually write the code.

news.headline: Baidu releases free open-source OCR model that reads 100-page PDFs in one pass
news.body: OCR (Optical Character Recognition, turning scanned documents into text) has always been painful. You split PDFs into chunks, process each page, stitch it back together. Baidu just killed that workflow. Unlimited-OCR reads an entire multi-page PDF in a single pass. No splitting. No stitching. One call, done. Here is what makes it actually usable: Cloud OCR bills you per page. This runs locally, forever, for free. You can drop it into any data pipeline to extract text from contracts, papers, or scanned archives without touching a paid API. 15,000+ GitHub stars already.
bullets: 3 billion parameters , runs on a single mid-range NVIDIA GPU, no beefy server needed
Handles multi-language documents without extra setup, outperforms DeepSeek-OCR on standard benchmarks
32,768-token output window , so even 100-page contracts fit in one shot
Plugs into Transformers, vLLM, or SGLang, tools you already know
MIT license, free weights on Hugging Face, zero API costs
